Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to Paisalo Digital Limited Q2 FY27 Earnings 
Conference Call hosted by Elara Securities (India) Private Limited. Before we begin, let me 
draw your attention to the fact that today's discussion may include certain forward-looking 
statements, which are predictions, projections or other estimates about future events. These 
statements reflect management's current expectations about future performance of the company 
and are subject to various risks and uncertainties that may cause actual results to differ 
materially. 
 
As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode and there will be an 
opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance 
during this conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star then zero on your touchtone 
phone. Please note that this conference is being recorded. 
 
I now hand the conference call over to Mr. Maneet Khimawat from Elara Securities. Thank you 
and over to you, sir. 
Maneet Khimawat: 
Thank you. Hello and good evening, everyone. On behalf of Elara Securities, I thank you all for 
joining the Q2 FY27 Earnings Conference Call of Paisalo Digital Limited. Today from the 
management, we have: Mr. Santanu Agarwal, Deputy Managing Director; Mr. Harish Singh, 
CFO; and Mr. Gaurav Chaubey, Chief Business Officer. 
 
I will now hand over the call to Mr. Santanu for his opening remarks, post which we can open 
the floor for question and answers. Thank you and over to you, sir. 
Santanu Agarwal: 
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today for Paisalo Digital's earnings call 
for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. I hope you have had the opportunity to review our 
earnings presentation, which has been shared earlier on the exchanges and is also available on 
our website. 
 
We are pleased to share that Paisalo has delivered another quarter of healthy performance with 
continued progress across growth, distribution, technology and asset quality. More importantly, 
the investments we have made over the past several quarters are increasingly translating into 
operating outcomes, reinforcing our confidence in scalability and resilience of our business 
model. 
 
Let me begin with a brief perspective on the operating environment. The Indian economy 
continues to demonstrate resilience despite global uncertainties supported by healthy domestic 
demand and broad-based economic activity. The RBI has maintained a constructive outlook 
revising its FY27 real GDP growth estimate to 7.1% in its latest monetary policy while the recent 
25 basis point repo rate increase reflects a calibrated approach to inflation management. At the 
same time, uneven monsoon conditions have affected sentiment in certain regions and rainfall 
deficit pockets warrant continued monitoring. 
 
Against this backdrop, we remain focused on balancing growth opportunities with disciplined 
risk management. Our diversified portfolio provides an important degree of resilience in this 

 
 
Paisalo Digital Limited 
 
 
October 22, 2026 
 
 
Page 3 of 12 
 
 
environment. Agri and allied segments account for approximately 15% of the portfolio while the 
balance diversified across food and hospitality, street vendors, health care, education, 
technology, manufacturing, textiles, transport and other SME and micro enterprise activities. 
 
Our geographical presence across 23 states and more than 10,000 pin codes provides significant 
diversification and granularity, reducing concentration risk while creating access to a vast 
underserved market opportunity. 
 
Over the past several quarters, we have continued to strengthen our technology and risk 
management capabilities. Our proprietary underwriting framework combines on-ground 
engagement with geospatial intelligence, alternate data and AI-driven analytics while our AI-
enabled portfolio monitoring platform provides real-time visibility, early warning indicators and 
dynamic risk assessment. These capabilities are reflected in the health of our portfolio with 
collection efficiency at 98.3%, gross NPA at 0.66% and net NPA at 0.46% at the end of the 
quarter. This gives us confidence in our ability to scale while maintaining disciplined asset 
quality. 
 
During the first half of this fiscal year, we have made significant progress in broadening and 
diversifying our access to capital markets. We have successfully raised approximately INR294.9 
crores through our public NCD issuance under the INR900 crores shelf program followed by 
INR124.47 crores listed dual-rated unsecured private placement of NCDs in September. We 
have also raised over INR177 crores through commercial paper issuances during H1 FY27 
further 
enhancing 
our 
funding 
flexibility 
and 
liquidity 
position.  
 
A significant portion of this funding was raised towards the end of the quarter, which temporarily 
impacted reported yields. We expect yields to normalize and the incremental interest income 
contribution to progressively follow through. At the same time, the enhanced balance sheet 
capacity provides greater headroom for an improvement in RoE as deployment scales up. 
Supported by strong capitalization, increasing operating leverage, a rapidly expanding 
distribution network and accelerating digital orientation, Paisalo is well positioned to capitalize 
on the strong demand environment. The festive season, resilient consumption trends and 
continued execution across our platform provides a solid foundation for sustained growth. 
 
Let me now turn to our broader strategy. Our growth is anchored around four reinforcing pillars: 
distribution, product diversification, technology and AI and liability management. As each of 
these capabilities scale, they are reinforcing one another and strengthening the quality, efficiency 
and resilience of the franchise. 
 
Distribution remains at the heart of our growth strategy. During Q2, our footprint expanded to 
6,415 touchpoints across 23 states comprising 426 branches, 4,299 distribution points and 1,690 
business correspondents touchpoints. Importantly, our expansion combines a branch-led 
presence with an increasingly asset-light distribution model enabling us to deepen penetration 
in existing markets while expanding into new and contagious geographies. Our customer 

 
 
Paisalo Digital Limited 
 
 
October 22, 2026 
 
 
Page 4 of 12 
 
 
franchise has correspondingly scaled to approximately 20 million providing a significantly 
larger base for future growth and engagement. 
 
Our Business Correspondent network is an important strategic component of this distribution 
architecture. Partnerships with State Bank of India, Bank of India and Indian Overseas Bank 
give us last mile connectivity across underserved markets and deepen our participation in the 
formal financial ecosystem. During Q2, the BC network expanded to 1,690 touchpoints and 
served approximately 1.93 million customers across services ranging from account opening, 
fund transfer to social security products and micro credit. Importantly, we see this channel as 
more than a transaction network. Over time, it can create a broader customer ecosystem for 
Paisalo and strengthen the foundation of future credit acquisition and cross-sell. 
 
Our second pillar is product diversification. As the distribution franchise scales, the opportunity 
is not simply to reach more customers, but to address a broader range of financing needs within 
the ecosystems where we already operate. We, therefore, intend to progressively broaden our 
product suite around the core MSME and micro entrepreneurs franchise through an increasingly 
partnership-led and asset-light approach. This should allow us to improve distribution, 
productivity, diversify our growth avenues and deepen customer engagement while maintaining 
disciplined underwriting. 
 
Our third pillar is Technology and AI where we continue to make meaningful progress. During 
Q2, AI-enabled onboarding processed approximately 1.90 lakh applications while AI-driven 
outbound calling scaled to approximately 3 lakh calls daily. We now have 25 live AI bots across 
the organization. More importantly, AI is increasingly embedded across the lending life cycle 
from sourcing and onboarding to underwriting, portfolio monitoring, collections and customer 
engagement. 
 
These capabilities are helping improve turnaround times, strengthen monitoring and reduce 
manual intervention. We are also beginning to see these investments translate into operating 
efficiency. Despite 33% year-on-year growth in AUM and continued expansion of our network, 
our employee base declined by 11% year-on-year during the quarter. We see this as an early 
evidence of increasing operating leverage as technology and automation enables us to scale 
business volumes without a commensurate increase in operating resources. 
 
Our fourth pillar is liability management where the focus remains on diversification, funding 
flexibility and cost efficiency. The progress made through public and private NCD issuances, 
commercial paper and proactive debt management has broadened our funding architecture 
during the first half. As Paisalo scales, this increasingly diversified liability franchise should 
provide greater flexibility in funding growth while supporting balance sheet efficiency.  
 
Taken together, our progress across distribution, product diversification, technology and funding 
is strengthening the scalability and resilience of our franchise.

We believe Paisalo is well positioned for the next phase of growth. The platform we have built 
across distribution, products, technology and funding is stronger and more scalable today giving 
us the ability to pursue significantly larger opportunities while remaining disciplined on risk, 
capital and returns. We thank our investors and stakeholders for their continued trust and support 
as we build a more resilient technology-led and financially inclusive company. 
 
With that, let me hand over the call to Mr. Gaurav Chaubey, our CBO, to share his perspective 
on the operating environment before we move to the detailed financial performance. Thank you. 
Gaurav Chaubey: 
Good afternoon and thank you. Let me share our perspective on the operating environment, the 
areas where we are seeing some pressure and importantly, the actions we are taking to protect 
portfolio 
quality 
while 
continuing 
to 
capture 
attractive 
growth 
opportunities.  
 
The 2026 Southwest monsoon ended at about 87% of the long period average with considerable 
regional variation. Even so, kharif sowing is down only by about 1% year-on-year and covers 
101% of normal acreage as irrigation and stable reservoir levels have helped offset the rainfall 
shortfall in most regions. 
 
The pressure is concentrated in certain pockets with Maharashtra the most impacted state this 
season and parts of Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana also receiving patchy below 
average rainfall. Certain districts have been declared drought affected. Customer demand in 
these areas has been relatively muted and we have responded by tightening underwriting 
guardrails, moderating rural disbursements in drought-related districts and stepping up 
collection efforts in these locations. 
 
Bihar experienced higher than expected rainfall in the latter part of the monsoon along with 
flooding in certain areas. Given our relatively limited portfolio exposure in the region, we 
currently expect the overall impact on our portfolio to remain manageable. 
 
For agri equipment finance in agrarian belt, repayments are typically structured at half yearly 
installments around the end of rabi and kharif season so it is still early to draw definitive 
conclusions on portfolio performance. We have also moderated our B2B business in certain 
drought affected markets across both urban and rural locations acting proactively wherever early 
cohort indicators began to move. 
 
Looking ahead, rural indicators remain broadly supportive with vehicle registrations in rural and 
semi-urban areas growing at marginally higher pace than in urban and metro markets during the 
first half. The kharif outcome should become clear by end of October or early November and 
we expect rural cash flows to improve after the harvest. State and central governments have been 
proactive in drought-affected areas, which should help soften the impact on rural households. 
Early October business momentum has been encouraging and the overall collection efficiency 
in our rural business portfolio continues to remain high. 

 
 
Paisalo Digital Limited

Despite seasonal backdrop, demand remains visible in mobility, machinery and other movable 
asset financing in Maharashtra supported by industrial and urban activity. In Uttar Pradesh, 
demand remains healthy across mobility and agricultural segments while Haryana and Rajasthan 
are seeing opportunities in machinery and mobility financing supported by manufacturing, 
mining, construction, infrastructure and agricultural mechanization. Delhi and NCR continues 
to see broad-based credit demand across commercial, trade, transport and service activities. 
 
More broadly, we are seeing an uptick in credit offtake among MSME and SME borrowers 
across several emerging markets driven by working capital and business expansion needs.  
 
Overall, while we remain watchful in specific rural and agricultural pockets, the broader demand 
environment remains supportive. Our approach is to stay agile, calibrating growth at the cohort 
and geographical level while preserving underwriting and collection discipline. 
 
With that, let me hand over to Mr. Harish Singh, our Executive Director and CFO, to take you 
through the financial performance in greater detail. Thank you.

as of September 30, 2026 while net NPA improved by 19 basis points to 0.46%. Collection 
Efficiency stood at 98.3%. Credit cost declined to 0.4% in quarter 2 financial year '27 compared 
with 1.1% in quarter 2 financial year '26. While H1 financial year '27 loan losses and provision 
declined by 47% year-on-year to INR155 million from INR295 million in H1 financial year '26. 
 
Turning to the balance sheet. Total borrowings stood at INR54,808 million as of September 30, 
2026. Our Cost of Borrowing declined by approximately 50 basis points year-on-year to 10% 
reflecting the continued diversification of our liability franchise. Debt-to-equity stood at 2.89x 
while capital adequacy remained healthy at 30.7%, including Tier 1 capital of 25.2%. Our ALM 
position remained comfortable with a positive gap across buckets. 
 
As we enter the second half of financial year '27, our priorities remain focused on sustaining 
growth, improving funding efficiency, maintaining asset quality discipline and translating the 
increasing scale of the franchise into sustainable returns and long-term value for all our 
stakeholders. Our balance sheet and capital position provide us with the capacity to support this 
next phase of growth while maintaining financial discipline. 
 
Thank you. With that, let me hand the call back to the moderator. 
Moderator: 
Thank you very much. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. First question is 
from the line of Sandy Mehta from Evaluate Research. 
Sandy Mehta: 
Congratulations on a very strong set of results across the board and well-done job on Investor 
Relations with your presentation in this conference call. My first question is with the RBI now 
raising rates, can you comment a little bit on how that will impact you in terms of lending and 
borrowing yields and your net interest margin? You mentioned that you have some borrowings 
at the end of the quarter and you expect your yields to normalize. But how do you think this 
plays out over the next few quarters, please? 
Santanu Agarwal: 
So, in terms of the RBI raising rates, as you might have heard in the recent statement also by the 
Honorable Governor, he said that he is not expecting any more rate cuts going forward for the 
next couple of quarters and there should be an incremental impact. I mean if you see the morning 
today, G-SEC also was up about 50 basis points. 
 
So we definitely expect that there is going to be about a 25 to 30 basis point increase, which we 
have already priced in. By the way, if you remember in quarter 1, we gave our full year guidance 
of finishing our cost of funds at 10.5%. And we are currently at the end of quarter 2 or half year 
1, we are standing at 10%. So that cushion is definitely built into the system. 
Sandy Mehta: 
Okay. And so you do expect your Net Interest Margins to rebound a bit over the balance of the 
year? 
Santanu Agarwal: 
Yes. Net Interest Margins will be range bound within the expectation which was provided, which 
was about 6% on an annualized basis. We are currently at 5.7%. So definitely, irrespective of

whether we go from 10% to 10.25% or 10.5% in terms of the cost of funds, we are definitely 
expecting the NIMs to close at about 6%. 
 
Also, when you look at Q2 in general, you see that there has been other activities also where you 
see that due to the tariff practice and the drought affected areas, there have been certain issues 
that propped up on the portfolio in terms of growth. And all the capital raise, which took place 
along all the debt and everything, was towards the end of the quarter, which on a transient basis 
created a denominator effect, which reduced the yields. 
Sandy Mehta: 
Okay. You mentioned that the head count was down 11%, which is just -- I think it's remarkable 
given the overall growth of the organization. So do you expect more operational efficiency going 
forward? Are there any metrics or any quantification of that going forward? 
Santanu Agarwal: 
No. So, as I continue to say that all the reduction in the workforce that you even saw in the last 
quarter, we reduced the workforce by about 3% despite an AUM growth of about 27%, 28-odd 
percent, was a factor of our existing distribution network, which we have been working for the 
last few years maturing and spearing out incremental disbursements and the product 
diversification that is taking place due to the asset-light expansion of the touchpoint franchise. 
 
So on a short-term basis, yes, it looks like it's going to sustain. But towards as we move into the 
festive season of Q3 and towards the end of quarter 4, we are expecting it to normalize. So, what 
you are seeing is an impact of what we have been spending our time and energy on for the last 
2 fiscal years in terms of our distribution strategy and product diversification strategy. 
 
I still continue to maintain the same wherein in the medium to long term with everything that 
we are doing with AI and all the new systems which are coming in place, in fact as guided in the 
last quarter, we are also releasing our app by the end of this Q3 to be targeting in Q4. We are 
going to have a little bit of a jump in our operating framework. 
Sandy Mehta: 
And one last question. Any update on the State Bank SBI co-lending business from their side in 
terms of approvals? And are there any other government regulations or changes in regulations 
that might impact your co-lending business? 
Santanu Agarwal: 
So we are pretty much status quo on the co-lending side of the business wherein that we are 
doing a little bit of co-lending here and there with all the banks. But most of -- we have complied, 
like I always say that we are in compliance with the entire circular. We are just waiting the go-
ahead from the respective banks as to whenever they are able to comply with their side of the 
circular. 
 
They have to create a CIF structure. They have to place it in their CBS. It's a long policy, long 
compliance side from their side. So we are good to go whenever they are ready with the same. 
So it's status quo right now from their side. 
Moderator: 
Next question is from the line of Manav from Antique Stock Broking Limited.

Manav: 
I have two questions. Firstly, how much of the yield moderation is purely the timing of 
disbursements versus the changes in product mix or competitive pricing? And secondly, our 
head count has declined 11% year-on-year despite the 33% AUM growth. So just checking how 
much further efficiency can tech deliver without affecting, let's say, customer service or

Santanu Agarwal: 
Manav, so with regard to your point on yields, it was mostly that yield factor was coming because 
a majority of the disbursement that took from the transition of quarter 1 to quarter 2 happened 
towards the end of the quarter of the quarter 2, which created a denominator effect temporarily 
affecting yields. 
 
Towards Q3 and Q4, yields will be back to normal. They will be normalized and we continue to 
maintain the same yield levels across our products and geographies that we are expanding into. 
So there is nothing that we are doing in terms of yield reduction just to enter a specific geography 
or a product. 
 
So this is just a temporary transient measure that took place on the same as told to you wherein 
a significant amount of funding and deployment was done towards the end of the quarter. So 
this is just a temporary impact on the reported yields. In terms of your headcount reduction point, 
we did reduce our head count last quarter also about 3% on a year-on-year basis despite giving 
about a 28% growth in the AUM. Obviously this time we have reduced it by 11% on a year-on-
year basis and giving a 33% AUM growth. 
 
This you are seeing because of the investments that we have been doing in the last 2 years 
towards product diversification and diversification of our touchpoints wherein we have been 
able to scale doubling of our touchpoints every year on -- and in fact one of these years, we were 
able to double it every quarter, right? 
 
So, what you are seeing is those operating leverages, which were laid in the last 2 years, now 
maturing and spewing disbursements for us. On a medium- to long-term basis as we release our 
application this quarter end also, which is quarter 3 end, and we have the new AI framework and 
franchises kicking in, we will see an increase in the operating leverage. This is just a temporary 
transient impact on a short-term basis.

So, my first question is management has previously spoken about leveraging AI and digital

bots that are live and we did about 3 lakh outbound calls on a daily basis. Now if you compare

But right now what is happening is we are having an AI framework also and we are having our 
touch framework also, which is a human operating leverage that we have, running on a combined 
basis where we are shifting a lot of load to AI, but there is still a maker checker framework, 
which is in place to ensure that AI is not on a stand-alone basis taking over the operations of the 
company, which is causing that blip in the operating leverage. So on a short-term basis, you will 
see that growth will outpace what we are doing here. 
 
But on a medium- to long-term basis that is when we approach quarter 1 of next fiscal year, you

leverage.

Santanu Agarwal: 
So we are -- our original acquisition strategy that we run on currently is called a High-tech, 
High-touch strategy where we are basically using a combination of services spread between
